46165-the-book-of-daniel-unlocked.title: The Book of Daniel Unlocked
46165-the-book-of-daniel-unlocked.creator: Unknown
46165-the-book-of-daniel-unlocked.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. There is one paragraph in it to which the Assyriologist is now able to add a few words. Auchincloss draws attention to the sense of completeness and perfection which is associated in the Old Testament, not only with the number seven, but also with the number ten. It has long been known that the Babylonians possessed a week of seven days.

arxiv-2206-12094.title: Unified BERT for Few-shot Natural Language Understanding
arxiv-2206-12094.creator: Junyu Lu, Ping Yang, Ruyi Gan, Jing Yang, Jiaxing Zhang
arxiv-2206-12094.description: Abstract Even as pre-trained language models share a semantic encoder, natural language understanding suffers from a diversity of output schemas. In this paper, we propose UBERT, a unified bidirectional language understanding model based on BERT framework, which can universally model the training objects of different NLU tasks through a biaffine network.

arxiv-2306-13687.title: Isometries and the double copy
arxiv-2306-13687.creator: Damien A. Easson, Gabriel Herczeg, Tucker Manton, and Max Pezzelle
arxiv-2306-13687.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Damien A. Easson, Gabriel Herczeg, Tucker Manton, and Max Pezzelle. In the standard derivation of the Kerr-Schild double copy, the geodicity of the Kerr-Schild vector and the stationarity of the spacetime are presented as assumptions that are necessary for the single copy to satisfy Maxwell’s equations.

arxiv-2310-05304.title: GestSync: Determining who is speaking without a talking head
arxiv-2310-05304.creator: Sindhu B Hegde, Andrew Zisserman
arxiv-2310-05304.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a new synchronisation task, Gesture-Sync : determining if a person’s gestures are correlated with their speech or not. In comparison to Lip-Sync, Gesture-Sync is far more challenging as there is a far looser relationship between the voice and body movement than there is between voice and lip motion.

arxiv-2404-13163.creator: Alireza Javadian Sabet, Sarah H. Bana, Renzhe Yu, Morgan R. Frank
arxiv-2404-13163.description: Abstract Higher education plays a critical role in driving an innovative economy by equipping students with knowledge and skills demanded by the workforce. While researchers and practitioners have developed data systems to track detailed occupational skills, such as those established by the U.S.

arxiv-2501-00170.title: Federated Learning with Workload Reduction through Partial Training of Client Models and Entropy-Based Data Selection
arxiv-2501-00170.creator: Hongrui Shi, Valentin Radu, Po Yang
arxiv-2501-00170.description: Abstract With the rapid expansion of edge devices, such as IoT devices, where crucial data needed for machine learning applications is generated, it becomes essential to promote their participation in privacy-preserving Federated Learning (FL) systems. The best way to achieve this desiderate is by reducing their training workload to match their constrained computational resources.

arxiv-2501-16627.title: Engaging with AI: How Interface Design Shapes Human-AI Collaboration in High-Stakes Decision-Making
arxiv-2501-16627.creator: Zichen Chen University of California, Santa Barbara zichen_chen@ucsb.edu, Yunhao Luo University of California, Santa Barbara yunhaoluo@ucsb.edu, Misha Sra University of California, Santa Barbara sra@ucsb.edu
arxiv-2501-16627.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zichen Chen University of California, Santa Barbara zichen_chen@ucsb.edu, Yunhao Luo University of California, Santa Barbara yunhaoluo@ucsb.edu, Misha Sra University of California, Santa Barbara sra@ucsb.edu. As reliance on AI systems for decision-making grows, it becomes critical to ensure that human users can appropriately balance trust in AI suggestions with their own judgment, especially in high-stakes domains like healthcare.

arxiv-2506-15078.title: Enhancing Vector Quantization with Distributional Matching: A Theoretical and Empirical Study
arxiv-2506-15078.creator: Xianghong Fang Litao Guo Hengchao Chen Yuxuan Zhang XiaofanXia, Dingjie Song Yexin Liu Hao Wang Harry Yang Yuan Yuan Qiang Sun
arxiv-2506-15078.description: Abstract The success of autoregressive models largely depends on the effectiveness of vector quantization, a technique that discretizes continuous features by mapping them to the nearest code vectors within a learnable codebook. Two critical issues in existing vector quantization methods are training instability and codebook collapse.

arxiv-2507-21339.title: Iwasawa Theory of Elliptic Curves in Quadratic Twist Families
arxiv-2507-21339.creator: Debanjana Kundu, Katharina Müller
arxiv-2507-21339.description: Abstract . In this article, we use two different approaches – one algebraic and the other analytic – to study the variation of Iwasawa invariants of rational elliptic curves in some quadratic twist families. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 11R23, 11G05; Secondary: 11R11, 11R45 1.

arxiv-2510-10344.title: A revision of the lifetime of submoons: tidal dynamics with the Euler-Lagrange equation
arxiv-2510-10344.creator: Iason Saganas 1, Grant Mayberry 2, Barbara Ercolano 3,4
arxiv-2510-10344.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Iason Saganas 1, Grant Mayberry 2, Barbara Ercolano 3,4. Submoons, moons orbiting other moons, may be exotic environments capable of hosting extraterrestrial life. We extend previous studies to revise the maximum lifetime of these objects due to planetary, lunar and sublunar tidal migration.

arxiv-2602-21979.title: Quantum criticality in open quantum systems from the purification perspective
arxiv-2602-21979.creator: Yuchen Guo, Shuo Yang
arxiv-2602-21979.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yuchen Guo, Shuo Yang. Open quantum systems host mixed-state phases that go beyond the symmetry-protected topological and spontaneous symmetry-breaking paradigms established for closed, pure-state systems. Developing a unified and physically transparent classification of such phases remains a central challenge. In this work, we introduce a purification-based framework that systematically characterizes all mixed-state phases in one-dimensional systems with ℤ 2 σ × ℤ 2 τ \mathbb{Z}_{2}^{\sigma}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{\tau} symmetry.

pmc-11310016.title: First-line immune checkpoint inhibitors in low programmed death-ligand 1-expressing population
pmc-11310016.creator: Feiyang Zhang, Guoming Chen, Yixin Yin, Xiaojiang Chen, Runcong Nie, Yingbo Chen
pmc-11310016.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Inhibitors of programmed cell death 1 (PD1) and its ligand (PDL1) have exhibited favorable long-term survival in many types of advanced-stage cancer and current approvals have to date been granted in certain tumour types irrespective of PD-L1 status. Methods: We extracted the following information: study sample size, trial period, cancer types, intervention of treatment, type of PD-L1 antibody, immunohistochemistry (IHC) scoring method, number and percentage of PD-L1 < 1% population, and median follow- up time.

pmc-11443673.title: Association of single bolus versus bolus followed by infusion of tranexamic acid with blood loss in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis surgery
pmc-11443673.creator: Mohd Shahnaz Hasan, Mew Har Leong, Zheng-Yii Lee, Chee Kidd Chiu, Chris Yin Wei Chan, Mun Keong Kwan, Siti Nadzrah Yunus
pmc-11443673.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAdolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) corrective surgery may involve significant blood loss and blood transfusion requirements. Antifibrinolytic agents such as tranexamic acid (TXA) have been used to reduce blood loss, but its optimal dose is uncertain.

pmc-11495872.title: Postpartum hepatitis flares in mothers with chronic hepatitis B infection
pmc-11495872.creator: Shi OuYang, Yawen Geng, Gongqin Qiu, Yueying Deng, Haitao Deng, Calvin Q Pan
pmc-11495872.description: Postpartum elevation of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) in mothers with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) presents a significant clinical challenge. However, the existing literature demonstrates inconsistencies regarding its incidence and predictors in mothers infected with the hepatitis B virus (HBV). Recent advancements in antiviral prophylaxis against mother-to-child transmission of HBV and postpartum cessation of antiviral therapy further complicate this issue.

pmc-11574166.title: PSO-NMPC control strategy based path tracking control of mining LHD (scraper)
pmc-11574166.creator: Ya Liu, Ping-an Peng, Li-guan Wang, Jia-xi Wu, Ming-yu Lei, Chao-wei Zhang, Ru Lei
pmc-11574166.description: The automation of underground articulated vehicles is a critical step in advancing digital and smart mining. Current nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) controllers face challenges such as delays in turning on large curvature paths and correction lags during the control of underground the Load-Haul-Dump (LHD).

pmc-12719171.title: FeCuCe trimetallic nanoalloys exhibiting superior peroxidase activity for colorimetric detection of total antioxidant capacity
pmc-12719171.creator: Fang Wang, Xiuhui Zeng, Meiting Fu, Fanjun Lin, Haixia Li, Chenchen Li, Lifang Gao
pmc-12719171.description: Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) serves as a valuable parameter for evaluating the quality of natural foods and plants. We report the synthesis of FeCuCe nanoalloys with a high density of uniformly distributed catalytic sites that function as efficient peroxidase-like nanozymes for sensitive colorimetric TAC detection.

pmc-13216763.title: Acute Motor Axonal Neuropathy Coexisting With Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Case‐Based Review
pmc-13216763.creator: Yiğit Can Güldiken, Batool Achmar, Sema Kaymaz Tahra
pmc-13216763.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Guillain‐Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by peripheral nerve involvement. Among the many kinds of GBS, acute motor axonal neuropathy (AMAN) syndrome has been shown to have distinct clinical characteristics and consequences. Meanwhile, ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a long‐term inflammatory joint illness that mostly affects the sacroiliac joints and the spine; this disorder has been known to cause discomfort and stiffness, which may lead to decreased flexibility over time.

pmc-13238529.creator: Ronan M. G Berg, Colleen S Deane, Jill N Barnes, Harry B Rossiter
pmc-13238529.description: itiative launched in 2007 by the American College of Sports Medicine in partnership with the American Medical Association. The Exercise is Medicine® initiative primarily aims to address physical inactivity by encouraging clinicians to promote or prescribe exercise within routine care pathways (Sallis, 2009).

pmc-13518962.title: Clonal memory of cell division in humans diverges between healthy haematopoiesis and acute myeloid leukaemia
pmc-13518962.creator: Alessandro Donada, Gurvan Hermange, Tiziana Tocci, Adil Midoun, Giulio Prevedello, Louisa Hadj Abed, Délia Dupré, Wenjie Sun, Idan Milo, Sabrina Tenreira Bento, Constandina Pospori, Andrew J Innes, Christophe Willekens, Jacques Vargaftig, David Michonneau, Cristina Lo Celso, Nicolas Servant, Ken R D
pmc-13518962.description: Clonal memory, a cellular property inherited across at least two divisions, is a key driver of cell heterogeneity. To uncover its roles in human haematopoiesis, we develop high-resolution ex vivo tools that track both division and fate commitment of individual primary human haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs).

pmc-13682407.title: High-fat diet-derived metabolite uridine diphosphate (UDP) impairs epithelial regeneration by P2Y 6 -receptor signaling
pmc-13682407.creator: Rebecca Springer, Philip Claus, Marius Hörner, Christoph Otto, Natalie Burkard, Jakob Lauerer, Hanna Deinlein, Agnes Fekete, Werner Schmitz, Florian Seyfried, Nicolas Schlegel
pmc-13682407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Obesity is associated with a chronic low-grade inflammation affecting metabolic changes and organ dysfunction. Impairment of the intestinal epithelial barrier (IEB) and alterations in gut microbiota are considered to contribute to this phenotype by largely undefined mechanisms. Here, we used a diet-induced obesity model in rats to investigate the early interplay between a high-fat diet (HFD), gut microbiota composition, metabolic stool contents and IEB regeneration. Male Wistar rats received either a high-fat diet or a low-fat diet (LFD) ad libitum.
